exercise.name: Lever Incline Hammer Chest Press

reference.title: Lever Incline Hammer Chest Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Plate-loaded incline press (iso-lateral lever arms, neutral handles)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles come down, breathe out as you press up and forward.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: start with light plates on the horns and press with the back on the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit back on the reclined pad with the feet flat; neutral grip (palms facing each other) on the vertical handles; arms extended up and forward.
Breathe in and lower the handles along the arc to the upper chest, elbows about 45 degrees from the trunk.
Pause with the hands beside the upper chest; shoulder blades back and down on the pad.
Breathe out and press up and forward until the arms are long.
Squeeze the upper chest with the arms long; keep the head on the pad.

mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the handles start at the upper chest, not the neck.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about 45-60 degrees from the trunk.

mistakes.mistake: Back leaving the pad to push
mistakes.fix: Keep the back and head on the pad; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders rolling forward at the end
mistakes.fix: Stop with the arms long and the shoulder blades still on the pad.

kinematics.peak: ≈140° with the hands beside the upper chest
kinematics.norm: From well bent with the hands beside the chest to nearly straight (clinical opinion)
About 45-60 degrees from the trunk at the chest (clinical opinion)
Neutral: palms facing each other on vertical handles (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 144.2 cm high, -64 cm behind the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 21.2°; hands within 0.31 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handles ride an incline arc: up and forward from the upper chest (clinical opinion)
Back on the pad, little trunk work compared with free-weight or standing presses (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012)
Incline pressing raised the upper (clavicular) pectoralis compared with flat pressing; very steep inclines shift work to the front deltoid (Rodriguez-Ridao 2020; Lauver 2016)

kinematics.peak: 2 s back, 0.3 s pause, 1.3 s press
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s back and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5103, Lever Incline Hammer Chest Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)

Rodríguez-Ridao, Antequera-Vique, Martín-Fuentes and Muyor 2020, effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339; PMC7579505)
Lauver, Cayot and Scheuermann, influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise (Eur J Sport Sci, 2016; PubMed 25799093)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Load is user-chosen: start light and press without the back leaving the pad.
At the end of the set let the handles come back under control before letting go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the range so the hands stop in front of the chest.
Low back discomfort: keep both feet flat and the back on the pad.
progressions: Slower return with a pause at the chest.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Prime mover; the incline path favours the clavicular fibres (Rodriguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Prime mover; the incline path favours the clavicular fibres (Rodriguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Works more as the incline steepens (Lauver 2016).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Works more as the incline steepens (Lauver 2016).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Moves the shoulder blade forward at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.core: Little demand with the back on the pad (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2012).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Controls the elbow on the return.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Controls the elbow on the return.

phases.label: Handles down to the upper chest

guides.label: Up and forward along the arc
